title: Reporting what people say using nouns and adjectives
subtitle: the claim that ... / doubtful whether ...
summary: Report words and opinions with a noun or an adjective, and choose the clause or preposition that each one takes.

lesson.heading: Noun + that-clause
lesson.text: We can report with a **noun** in the reporting clause. Most of these nouns are related to reporting verbs (acknowledgement - acknowledge, statement - state). Also: advice, allegation, announcement, answer, argument, comment, decision, explanation, forecast, guarantee, indication, observation, promise, recommendation, reply, speculation, suggestion, threat, warning.

examples.text: The **claim** is often made **that** smoking causes heart disease.
The jury came to the **conclusion that** the woman was guilty.
I think it was Aristotle who made the **observation that** there's no such thing as bad publicity.

lesson.note: We do not usually leave out that after these nouns. Reporting with a noun or adjective does not claim to give the exact original words.

lesson.heading: Noun + to-infinitive clause
lesson.text: Some of these nouns are followed by a to-infinitive instead. Also: decision, instruction, order, promise, recommendation, refusal, threat, warning.

examples.text: I accepted Luisa's **invitation to visit** her in Rome.
He gave me every **encouragement to take up** painting again.
They carried out their **threat to dismiss** workers on strike.
examples.note: or ... their threat that they would dismiss workers on strike.

lesson.heading: Noun + of + wh-clause
lesson.text: Before a wh-clause these nouns normally need **of**. Also: discussion, explanation, problem.

examples.text: Juan raised the **question of when** the money would be collected.
Our previous meeting looked at the **issue of how** to increase income.
He failed to address the **question of who** would pay for the repairs.

lesson.heading: as to + wh-clause
lesson.text: After many of these nouns we can use **as to** to introduce the subject of a question or topic. Another preposition is usually possible instead.

examples.text: She asked my advice **as to what** subject she should study at university.
There was some discussion **as to whether** the price included tax or not.
Before we left we gave them strict instructions **as to how to cook** it.
examples.note: or ... about how to cook it.

left.label: Feelings and opinions: + that-clause
left.text: Also: adamant, agreed, angry, annoyed, grateful, insistent, sure.
examples: The builders are **certain that** they'll be finished by the end of next week.
The company is **adamant that** the child car seats are safe.
All the players are **agreed that** the game should go on.

right.label: Uncertainty: + wh-clause
right.text: Also: doubtful (usually + whether), uncertain, not certain, unsure.
examples: Scientists aren't **sure where** the remains of the satellite will land.
The climbers were **doubtful whether** the clothes would be warm enough.
Karim left in September but he was **not certain when** he would return.

lesson.heading: Adjective + preposition + noun phrase
rows: Rachel was extremely apologetic **about** turning up late.
Today's newspapers are very critical **of** the President's decision.
Hughes became abusive **to / towards** a police officer.

lesson.text: Sort the adjective first: opinion takes *that*, uncertainty takes a wh-word, and a reaction to a thing takes a preposition.

exercises.prompt: The turning point in his life came when he took the ___ to become an actor.
exercises.explanation: decision is a reporting noun and takes a to-infinitive (or a that-clause: the decision that he would become an actor).

exercises.prompt: Match each reporting noun with the clause that follows it.

pairs.left: The jury came to the conclusion

pairs.right: of when the money would be collected.
as to whether the price included tax.

exercises.prompt: I think it was Aristotle who made the observation ___ there's no such thing as bad publicity.
exercises.explanation: After a reporting noun we normally keep that.

exercises.prompt: He failed to address the question ___ who would pay for the repairs to the building.
exercises.explanation: Reporting nouns take of before a wh-clause.

exercises.prompt: The climbers were ___ the clothes would be warm enough at high altitudes.
exercises.explanation: Adjectives of uncertainty take a wh-clause, and doubtful is normally followed by whether.

exercises.prompt: My boss is very unsympathetic and was ___ my complaints about the new software.
exercises.explanation: dismissive, critical and scornful take of + noun phrase.

exercises.prompt: Rachel is normally very reliable and was extremely ___ turning up late.
exercises.explanation: apologetic, complimentary, insulting and tactful take about + noun phrase.

exercises.prompt: What follows each adjective when it reports what somebody said or felt?

exercises.statement: Scientists aren't sure that the remains of the satellite will land.
exercises.explanation: Scientists aren't sure where the remains of the satellite will land. An adjective expressing uncertainty needs a wh-clause.

exercises.prompt: For months people have wondered whether President Malik would stand again. There have been months of ___ as to whether he would stand again.
exercises.explanation: speculation is a reporting noun, and as to introduces the topic in formal writing.

exercises.prompt: Report that nobody has explained this. Put the words in order.
exercises.answer: There is still no definite explanation as to why the dinosaurs disappeared
exercises.explanation: explanation + as to + wh-clause is the formal reporting pattern with a noun.

exercises.statement: Today's newspapers are very critical of the President's decision to appoint Mr Walters.
exercises.explanation: Correct. critical takes of, and decision takes a to-infinitive.
